Hi Alex / Priya —

Thanks again for taking the time today. Quick recap of what we heard and the next steps we agreed on (so nothing gets lost):

What you told us (primary pains)
- Latency spikes when patients hit the triage flow during morning peak (60–90s currently for multi-step summarization).
- Cost per conversational session is unpredictable due to per-request cold starts and lack of prefix caching.
- Need structured outputs for the EHR ingestion (JSON schema) and a reranking layer for patient-clinician matching.

Goals
- Reduce median end-to-end latency to under 6s for the triage summary path.
- Ensure deterministic JSON outputs for downstream EHR ingestion.
- POC to evaluate embeddings+rerank for clinical note matching (target: +10% relevance uplift).

What Redwood proposes (high-level)
- Use our streaming function-calls for the triage flow to keep user-visible latency low while generating structured JSON in the background.
- Enable prefix/KV caching and continuous batching on the Dedicated pool to stabilize per-token cost and limit cold-starts.
- Run a 4-week pilot combining embeddings + reranker using your sample dataset.

Immediate next steps (owners & timing)
1) Spectral: share the minimal sample dataset (100 de-identified triage sessions) and the EHR JSON schema — due Thu 29 Jul (Alex).
2) Redwood (Marissa): provide a short SDK diff and sample redwood-sample-config.yaml for the streaming funcall flow — due Wed 28 Jul. (Attachment: redwood-sample-config.yaml)
3) Joint: schedule a 60m engineering sync to walk the SDK changes and address network/KMS questions — suggested slot Fri 30 Jul.
4) Commercial: proposed pilot SOW and pricing cadence (we'll share a draft after we validate the dataset).

Attachments: spectral-ma-questions.xlsx (we'll use to capture data schema + security Qs).

If that aligns, I'll loop in our solutions engineer (Marissa) on the dataset thread and book the sync.

Thanks —

Hi Alex / Priya — looping in Ben (solutions infra) and dropping the quick technical playbook we discussed. I included a short SDK diff below and a sample config (attached).

Key technical decisions we recommend for the POC
- Streaming + function-calls: emit incremental partial results to the client to keep perceived latency low. Final structured JSON will be provided as a function call completion event. This pattern preserves UX while ensuring a validated JSON object at completion.
- Prefix/KV caching: enable prefix caching for the triage primer prompts (we typically pin common system prompts and triage templates). The cache hits reduce token compute by ~30% for repeated flows.
- Continuous batching policy: set a max latency budget of 60ms for the batching window during peak. That usually hits the sweet spot between throughput and tail latency.
- Embeddings + reranker: use 768-d float16 embeddings for the initial POC then explore quantized 8-bit for Dedicated to cut cost.

Minimal SDK changes (example)
- Add a streaming funcall helper: Redwood.stream(sessionId, {onPartial, onComplete}) — see snippet below.
- Add automatic JSON schema validation hook for function-call returns: Redwood.validateSchema(schema, output)

Sample snippet:
--- redwood-sample-config.yaml ---
# model: redwood/fast-embed-1
streaming: true
function_call: true
cache:
  enabled: true
  prefix_keys:
    - triage_prompt_v1
batching:
  policy: continuous
  max_latency_ms: 60
---

Attachments: redwood-sample-config.yaml (attached), small checklist for SSO/KMS.
